title: Transport through the Cell Membrane
subject: Physiology
description: Transport through the cell membrane: passive transport, simple diffusion, and protein channels.

cards.cloze: Transport through the cell membrane occurs by {{passive}} or {{active}} transport.
Membrane Transport — Passive: {{Simple Diffusion}} (through {{Lipid Bilayer}} or {{Protein Channels}}: {{Leak}} or {{Gated}} → {{Voltage Gated}} / {{Ligand Gated}}) and {{Facilitated Diffusion}}.
Membrane Transport — Active: {{Primary Active}} and {{Secondary Active}} ({{Co-Transport}} and {{Counter Transport}}).

I- Passive Transport: Definition: It is the transport of molecules through the cell membrane from areas of {{high concentration}} to areas of {{low concentration}} (i.e., {{down concentration gradient}} or {{downhill}}) by the aid of the {{kinetic energy}} of the molecules.
Types of Passive transport: • {{Simple diffusion}} • {{Facilitated diffusion}}
1. Simple diffusion: Definition: It is the transport of substances either through: a- the {{lipid bilayer}} or b- through the {{channel proteins}} of the cell membrane.
a- Simple diffusion through the lipid bilayer: • {{Non-polar}} and {{lipid-soluble}} molecules e.g. {{oxygen}}, {{carbon dioxide}}, and {{fat-soluble vitamins}}.
i- oxygen diffuses from the {{blood}} into the {{cells}}. ii- carbon dioxide diffuses in the {{opposite direction}}.

b- Simple diffusion through protein channels: • Diffusion of {{small water soluble}} molecules e.g. {{electrolytes}} • The channels are {{highly selective}}: the {{sodium channel}} is specifically selective for passage of sodium ions. the {{potassium channel}} is selective for potassium transport.
Types of the channel according to presence or absence of a {{gate}}: 1- {{leak channels}}: {{continuously opened}}. 2- {{Gated channels}}: Controlled by {{gates}}.

a- {{Voltage gated}} ion channel: These channels open or close according to changes in {{membrane voltage (potential)}}. b- {{Chemical (ligand) gated}} ion channels: These channels open or close by binding to a {{ligand}}.
